Simple model build to familiarize myself with concepts. I was getting lost in the process doing the SP500. Will scale up after I get the basics down.

```{r}
#packages
library(tidyquant)
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
```

```{r}
# download market returns for portfolio --> lets just use 3-4 stocks to keep it simple
# [ (n^2 - n) / 2 ] + n days, where N = number stocks in portfolio
# GOOG, BG, RTX --> different sectors so have even less correlation (in theory)


goog <- tq_get("GOOG")
bg <- tq_get("BG")
rtx <- tq_get("RTX")

goog_1 <- goog |> mutate(daily_ret = ((adjusted - lag(adjusted))/lag(adjusted))*100)
bg_1 <- bg |> mutate(daily_ret = ((adjusted - lag(adjusted))/lag(adjusted))*100)
rtx_1 <- rtx |> mutate(daily_ret = ((adjusted - lag(adjusted))/lag(adjusted))*100)

head(goog_1)
head(bg_1)
head(rtx_1)
```


```{r}
returns_wide <- goog_1 |> select(date, GOOG = daily_ret) |>
  inner_join(bg_1 |> select(date, BG = daily_ret), by = "date") |>
  inner_join(rtx_1 |> select(date, RTX = daily_ret), by = "date") |>
  drop_na()
```

```{r}
#standarise the data. call it Z.
Z <- returns_wide |> select(-date) |> scale()
```

```{r}
# create correlation matrix from Z call it cor_Z. can skip cov step.
cor_Z <- cor(Z)
```

```{r}
# calculate eigenvalues and eigenvectors from corr_z
eigen <- eigen(cor_Z)

eigenvalues  <- eigen$values
eigenvectors <- eigen$vectors

var_explained     <- eigenvalues / sum(eigenvalues)
cum_var_explained <- cumsum(var_explained)
```

```{r}
# plot eigenvalues on line graph largest - smallest. x-axis; eigenvector #, y-axis; % variance explained
eigen_data <- data.frame(eigenvalue = eigenvalues, percent_var = var_explained * 100 
)

#order largest-smallest
eigen_data <- eigen_data[order(eigen_data$eigenvalue), ]

ggplot(eigen_data, aes(x = eigenvalue, y = percent_var)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue", size = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "red", size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "Eigenvalue vs. Percentage of Variance Explained",
    x = "Eigenvalue",
    y = "% Variance Explained"
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```
